## Ecology with practical consequences

The invasive yellow-legged hornet (*Vespa velutina*) poses ecological and economic challenges across Europe. My doctoral research investigated the role of the European honey-buzzard (*Pernis apivorus*) as a native predator of this invasive species.

We combined nest monitoring, camera traps, tracking devices, diet analysis, spatial modelling and ecosystem-service valuation. This work links predator behaviour to biological pest regulation and conservation decisions.

### Research questions

- How does the honey-buzzard exploit invasive hornets during the breeding season?
- Which breeding habitats and landscape features support its ecological functions?
- How can the biological and economic contribution of native predators be quantified?

### Selected publications

- [Integrating ecology and economics: European honey buzzards as ecosystem service providers against yellow-legged hornets](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecoser.2026.101912). *Ecosystem Services* (2026).

- [The European honey buzzard as an ally for invasive hornet control](https://doi.org/10.1002/ps.8622). *Pest Management Science* (2025).
